gpu_bf16_dense_flop.note: BF16 dense Tensor Core work only; 624 TFLOP/s sparsity peak does not apply. One multiply-add counts as 2 FLOPs.

gpu_fp32_flop.note: Keep FP32-layer work separate. Determine actual instruction path first; do not divide it by the BF16 peak. FP32 CUDA-core peak is 19.5e12 FLOP/s, TF32 is a different path.

gpu_hbm_bytes.note: Total HBM traffic, not model-file size or PCIe traffic. Decimal GB/s; theoretical peak, not measured bandwidth.

host_memory_bytes.note: Host RAM topology and bandwidth are unknown.

pcie_host_to_gpu_bytes.note: Actual host-to-GPU topology/link width unknown. 64 GB/s bidirectional must not be used as one-way capacity.

pcie_gpu_to_host_bytes.note: Actual GPU-to-host topology/link width unknown. Keep transfer directions explicit.

storage_read_bytes.note: Backing-storage read bandwidth is unknown; distinguish page-cache hits from physical reads.

network_bytes.note: External network path and bandwidth are unknown.

cpu_work.note: Choose a measured CPU operation definition and matching peak before supplying work.

notes: This template contains no MiniMax-H3 FLOP or byte estimates and predicts no generation time.
Add stage objects with id, depends_on, and work entries of {amount, unit}; null amount means unknown.
Use distinct stages for non-overlappable work and preserve true dependencies. A fused stage assumes ideal overlap among its resources.
Resource capacities describe shared resource pools. Do not duplicate one physical pool under different names to invent extra capacity.
Omitted resource work is assumed zero for the declared model. coverage=complete is an explicit assertion by the profiler, not automatic discovery.
Only use this full-GPU profile when the assigned GPU is the matching full A100, not a MIG slice.
GPU matrix, memory, launch, decode, I/O and transfer work still need profiling. Available RAM and VRAM capacity are feasibility constraints, not bandwidth.
